PART A

Where the calibration stands

The problem, the cohort fix, and the full setup matrix — the thirty-second version of everything before your part.

01 · The problem — deployed calibration at Addis

The deployed calibration reads y = 1.90x − 4.17 at MAC = 10.

ftir_17 · deployed_alldata_crossplotFTIR EC (y) vs HIPS Fabs/MAC (x); deployed predictions exist only for the fixed 190

This is the plot the whole project hangs on: the network calibration, carried to Addis, is steep with a deep negative intercept — at MAC = 6 it pivots to slope 1.14 but the intercept stays at −4.17 (that invariance is proved in part D). Nothing at Addis has negative EC; the offset is the model, not the air.

MAC 10 1.90x − 4.17 MAC 6 1.14x − 4.17 R² 0.76 · RMSE 1.49
02 · Ann's cohort — what "lowest OC/EC" means

Addis-like composition is the extreme tail of IMPROVE — 800 filters out of 13,010.

deck · filtering_by_ocecCutoff OC/EC ≤ 2.27; IMPROVE pool median 5.54

The Addis offset implies OC/EC far below anything IMPROVE routinely sees. Taking the 800 lowest-OC/EC filters (≤ 2.27 vs pool median 5.54) is the closest IMPROVE can get to Addis composition — and that cohort beats the deployed, smoke-906, no-selection and analog cohorts on both the Addis crossplot and a locked disjoint-site TOR test. Cohort engineering beyond this point breaks the TOR test, so this is the terminal IMPROVE-only candidate.

cutoff OC/EC ≤ 2.27 held-out TOR RMSE 3.4 vs random 4.4–7.3
03 · The setup matrix — every training choice, one table

Lowest-OC/EC + AIRSpec ends at −1.62 — and is the only setup robust to who processes it.

by_protocol/site_held_out · calibration_setup_matrixRow 1 is the entire IMPROVE network (13,010) — the only SPARTAN spectra we hold are ETAD's, used for evaluation only

Six training-set choices, one protocol per column set. The intercept ladder runs −4.17 (deployed) → −3.22 (lowest-OC/EC raw) → −1.62 (+ AIRSpec). The corrected setup is also the one whose answer barely moves between the group's Calibration-app protocol and our site-held-out protocol (−1.65 vs −1.62), while raw setups swing by more than a µg/m³ on the component choice alone. It passes the disjoint-site TOR test cleanly (slope 1.01, R² 0.90).

corrected intercept −1.62 protocol-robust −1.65 / −1.62 held-out TOR 1.01x · R² 0.90
PART B

Your baselining suggestion, implemented

AIRSpec, ported and validated, applied to all 13,634 pool spectra and Addis. Why it moves the answer — and Ann's question about it.

04 · AIRSpec 1/3

At the CH band, ~91% of a raw Addis spectrum is background, not chemistry.

deck · airspec_1_baselineOne real filter (median-like on all four bands and baseline height); grey = all 239 Addis spectra. Not an average.

The black line is a single real filter; the red dash is the smoothing-spline baseline AIRSpec fits underneath it, per spectrum. The shaded sliver is all that is actually bands. A PLS model on raw spectra is handed a predictor that is mostly background, and is free to lean on it. Port note: APRLssb reimplemented in Python and validated against your group's R output on the ETAD scans to ≤6×10⁻⁷ absorbance — this is your algorithm, not an approximation. EDF 6 vs 8 turned out indistinguishable (Δslope < 0.01).

CH-band baseline share ~91% port vs R ≤ 6×10⁻⁷ EDF 6 vs 8 Δslope < 0.01
05 · AIRSpec 2/3

What is left is a thin skin — the part the calibration should be reading.

deck · airspec_2_correctedSame single filter, baseline removed; the full plot spans 0.03 AU against a raw spectrum reaching 0.34

Same filter after subtracting its own baseline: O–H, the CH bands, carbonyl, and the 1600 band we keep arguing about. The whole panel spans three hundredths of an absorbance unit — the chemistry rides on a background ten times its size.

band signal ≈ 0.03 AU raw spectrum ≈ 0.34 AU
06 · AIRSpec 3/3 — why it matters for Addis specifically

Addis rides a higher background than the cohort it is calibrated against.

deck · airspec_3_background_gapBaseline height at 2920 cm⁻¹, one value per filter: 800 IMPROVE (purple), 239 Addis (red)

Median baseline at the CH band: 0.170 at Addis vs 0.101 in the lowest-OC/EC 800. Overlapping distributions — a shift in the centre, not a separation — but it means whatever a raw-spectra model learned about background does not transfer, and that error lands as an offset. Baselining both sides and retraining takes the Addis intercept from −3.22 to −1.62 and the slope from 1.59 to 0.86 at MAC = 10: the single biggest improvement of phase 3. Honest cost: Addis R² drops 0.77 → 0.66 and RMSE 1.16 → 2.41; we prefer it for its residual structure, not its fit (slide 09).

Addis baseline 0.170 cohort baseline 0.101 intercept −3.22 → −1.62
07 · Ann's question — doesn't the baseline carry EC?

The smoke calibration collapses on corrected spectra — its Addis response was mostly baseline.

by_protocol/site_held_out · crossplots_all_setupsAll six setups on identical per-panel square axes, fixed 190-filter cohort, MAC = 10

Ann's standing objection — EC's sloping absorption lives partly in the baseline, so baselining an EC calibration should lose signal — deserves a direct answer, and this is our evidence so far: the 906-smoke model falls from slope 2.65 to 0.37 when both sides are baselined, i.e. much of its raw response was background it had memorised; and the ftir_08 HIPS-transfer failure survives baselining, so what breaks at Addis is compositional, not a baseline artifact. The open question for you: how much genuine EC signal does the correction discard, and is a middle path (partial baseline retention, or your group's newer baselining work — Josh's method?) worth trying?

smoke-906 corrected slope 0.37 HIPS transfer post-AIRSpec still fails
PART C

What the models are actually leaning on

Two independent diagnostics land on the same quantity: site background. And the corrected model's remaining error is a clean constant.

08 · Component selection — interleaved vs site-held-out CV

What interleaved folds leak is the site's background, not its chemistry.

ftir_20 · component_selection_all_setups%RMSECV (log y) per cohort; solid = interleaved 10-fold, dashed = whole sites held out; blue = raw, red = 2nd derivative

Hold whole sites out and the error floor rises ×1.59 for biomass-smoke and ×1.41 for Ethiopia-shaped smoke — but only ×1.01–1.07 for the composition-selected cohorts. On 2nd-derivative spectra the entire effect vanishes (every ratio 0.89–1.06): removing the smooth baseline removes the advantage of having seen the site. Interleaved CV flatters exactly the cohorts the deployed family is built from. Same conclusion as the AIRSpec slides, reached from fold structure instead of spectra. Also: interleaved CV is row-order dependent (same 800 filters give k = 15/18/19 on reorderings; site-grouped gives k = 5 every time). Not a criticism of the app as a tool — it answers a different question than transfer to an unseen site.

smoke floor ×1.59 lowest-OC/EC ×1.01 2nd-deriv ratios 0.89–1.06
09 · Residual structure — raw vs corrected

The corrected model misses by a season-stable constant: −2.0 to −2.6 µg/m³.

ftir_15/22 · residual_vs_d2Residual vs Mahalanobis D² in score space; site-cluster bootstrap B = 200

The raw model's Addis error tracks extrapolation distance (r = 0.71) and flips sign by season (+0.49 Kiremt → −1.25 Dry) — it fails by being out of domain. The corrected model's error is D²-independent and sits at a flat −2.0 to −2.6 µg/m³ in every season. Bootstrap puts the corrected intercept at 95% CI [−1.78, −1.06] — excludes zero, disjoint from the raw model's [−4.88, −2.81]. A constant offset of that shape reads as a missing constant absorption component in HIPS Fabs, or a MAC/protocol mismatch — an external-anchor question, which is why cohort engineering stops here.

raw: resid ~ D² r = 0.71 corrected offset −2.0…−2.6 all seasons CI [−1.78, −1.06]
PART D

The MAC fork

MAC = 6 vs 10 is the deciding unknown — but it is a narrower question than it looks.

10 · Algebra first — what MAC can and cannot move

MAC cannot move any intercept — every calibration pivots; the fork is a slope contest.

ftir_19 · mac_slope_pivotx = Fabs/MAC, so switching MAC rescales x by a constant: intercept and R² exact, slope ×0.6 going 10 → 6

Since x = Fabs/MAC, changing MAC rescales the x-axis: every setup keeps its intercept and R² exactly and its slope scales by exactly 0.6. So the intercept ladder is MAC-proof, R² cannot arbitrate MAC, and the fork reduces to: MAC = 6 makes the raw models self-consistent (lowest-OC/EC 0.95, Ethiopia-shaped 1.05, deployed 1.14); MAC = 10 is where the corrected model lands (0.86). Two self-consistent branches; fit statistics cannot choose between them.

slope scaling ×0.6 exact raw @ MAC 6 0.95 corrected @ MAC 10 0.86
11 · The bridge — 151,843 IMPROVE filters

At Addis-like composition, IMPROVE's implied MAC is 10.05.

ftir_16 · improve_implied_mac_curveImplied MAC = HIPS Fabs / TOR EC, 151,843 matched filters, binned by OC/EC

Where IMPROVE has both HIPS and TOR, implied MAC has median 11.96 overall — and 10.05 in the Addis-like OC/EC ≤ 2.27 subset (n = 6,503). MAC = 10 is centred at Addis-like composition; MAC = 6 sits in the lower tail. The high-OC/EC tail's inflated implied MAC (median 19.8) independently shows Fabs carries organic-scaling non-EC absorption. Net phase-3 read: MAC ≈ 10, the corrected model, and a genuine non-EC absorption component at Addis — which is exactly what slide 09's constant offset looks like. We'd like your judgment on this chain, and whether a HIPS MAC/protocol bridge exists that could test it independently.

Addis-like subset MAC 10.05 pool median 11.96 high-OC/EC tail 19.8
PART E

The chemistry we need you for

The band identity, the seasonal split Ann asked for, and the in-country data that could anchor all of it.

12 · The ~1600 cm⁻¹ band

Not amine. Carboxylate and/or aromatic C=C — stuck below 1425 cm⁻¹ without your sub-1500 model.

ftir_12 · peak_center_1600_by_groupPeak centers under the edge-corrected window; unchanged on AIRSpec-corrected spectra

Addis peaks at 1617–1619 cm⁻¹ (IQR 1616–1620) in every season; every IMPROVE cohort sits ≥ 1633 with essentially no overlap. Within Addis the band co-varies with CH (ρ = 0.88) and carbonyl (0.93) but not with the 3100–3400 N–H/O–H window (0.17) — an N–H bend without its stretch is implausible, so amine is out. The remaining candidates, carboxylate COO⁻ and aromatic C=C, are both charcoal-consistent and cannot be separated on Teflon: the ~1400 symmetric partner is below AIRSpec's trusted range. Two asks: where does the sub-1500 model stand, and can we get Emily Lee's charcoal spectra as data (the paper versions are print-only)?

Addis center 1617–1619 IMPROVE ≥ 1633 ρ(1600, N–H window) 0.17
13 · Naveed's seasons — and Ann's next ask

Season changes loading, not shape — the next notebook predicts dry and wet separately.

ftir_17 · addis_spectra_by_seasonDry Oct–Feb / Belg Mar–May / Kiremt Jun–Sep; 43 of 296 spectra lack dates and are excluded

All bands, deployed EC (3.3 → 7.2 µg/m³) and Fabs (43 → 56 Mm⁻¹) peak in Kiremt, while the 1600-band centre never moves; the one shape effect is relatively more broad O–H in the Dry season. Ann's working hypothesis is that the dry, diesel-leaning aerosol is roughly right and the wet, charcoal-dominated seasons are what break — ftir_24 will put per-season crossplots under the locked models to test it. Consistent so far: the corrected model's offset is already season-stable, so if the split shows anything, it should show it in the raw models.

14 · Adama & Bishoftu — the uncomfortable check and the free test set

The one same-corridor TOR we have looks ordinary — and a second Ethiopian site sits unused.

context · adama_etbi_contextAdama Batch-54: 5 quartz filters, July 2024. ETBI (Bishoftu): 32 filters Oct–Dec 2025, 26 with HIPS Fabs

Adama TOR gives OC/EC 4.6–7.2 — right at the IMPROVE median, not the extreme tail the Addis offset implies regionally. Since Addis's "extreme" ranking is computed from the very FTIR/HIPS values under suspicion, we cannot currently tell how much of the extremity is the artifact. Reconciling Addis HIPS with FTIR OC at Adama-like composition would need MAC ≈ 47 m²/g — unphysical — so something has to give. ETBI (Bishoftu, median Fabs 26.9 Mm⁻¹ vs Addis 47.1) is an untouched in-country test set for every conclusion here — if its spectra come through in the same pull as INDH/CHTS.

Adama OC/EC 4.6–7.2 bridge MAC ≈ 47 m²/g ETBI 26 HIPS filters unused

Charcoal ATR — go / no-go

advice

Grinding stops at 10–40 µm; ambient soot is sub-micron. Is ATR on ground charcoal informative at all, or should we lean entirely on literature and your spectra?

What actually settles it

A co-located quartz-TOR campaign at ETAD or Bishoftu. Each sampling day separates MAC = 6 from MAC = 10 by ~3σ; 11–13 days per season (~36 filters total) reaches 5σ per season at half signal. It measures the extreme-EC hypothesis directly, anchors the non-EC-absorption read, and Adama Batch-54 already proves the sampling-and-analysis chain works. TOR needs quartz — archived Teflon cannot substitute.
